applies_why: The judge text addresses a collision involving the challenger's rows against D5 and finds it underdetermined, so K-C's chain-vs-chain method governs.
quote: D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] G answers the 'almah/bethulah and near-fulfillment rows, leaving the sign's sense open.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: The phrase 'leaving the sign's sense open' could mean either a forbidden demand for explicit verse wording or an underdetermination finding after CR2 G answers the rows; I read it as the latter because the judge says G answers the rows rather than applying the stating-verse test.
why: The judge text does not use the retired stating-verse test or decide by individual contrary verses; it notes CR2 G answers the challenger's rows and leaves the sign's sense underdetermined.
